It should let humans, workers, the Conversation Viewer, and approved public interfaces ask the same query of the same permitted corpus and receive reproducible, provenance-bearing results.\\n\\nThe design rule is **one search semantics, multiple clients**. Mersearch Core\\n\\nCurrent implementation: `tools/search_archive_content.py` (`Mercer_Searcher_1.0` historical/internal tool identity).\\n\\nCore owns:\\n- query parsing and Boolean semantics;\\n- `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses and implicit AND;\\n- quoted phrases;\\n- `NEAR` / `NEAR/n` with auditable token distance;\\n- field predicates;\\n- path/name glob semantics;\\n- record extraction from supported source formats;\\n- conservative notation-normalized math retrieval;\\n- exclusions / corpus boundary enforcement;\\n- provenance-bearing hit construction;\\n- deterministic sorting;\\n- topic enrichment and co-occurrence;\\n- machine-readable result generation.\\n\\nCore must remain usable without a web server or UI.\\n\\n### 2. Mersearch Index\\n\\nTarget layer. Precompute search-oriented representations without replacing source files:\\n- inventory/file manifest;\\n- record/message index;\\n- normalized lexical tokens;\\n- mathematical-expression inventory;\\n- source SHA-256 and source commit/ref;\\n- Viewer/document targets;\\n- conversation-family / duplicate-relation sidecars;\\n- explicit document→text-representation relations where provenance establishes them;\\n- topic/concept indexes;\\n- optional chronology summaries.\\n\\nGenerated indexes are derived state and must be rebuildable. They must never silently confer authority or suppress a source merely because another representation is newer/larger.\\n\\n### 3. Mersearch API / machine adapter\\n\\nTarget layer. A stable machine-facing wrapper over Core/Index for workers, Sites, Viewer and automation.\\n\\nMinimum request:\\n- query expression;\\n- corpus/profile;\\n- sort/order;\\n- pagination;\\n- requested facets;\\n- explain level.\\n\\nMinimum response:\\n- schema/tool/index versions;\\n- exact query and parsed representation;\\n- corpus/profile and exclusions;\\n- source/index commit identity;\\n- coverage counts;\\n- total hits before pagination;\\n- page/cursor;\\n- facets;\\n- hit records;\\n- per-hit provenance;\\n- match/explanation trace;\\n- warnings/limitations.\\n\\nAPI must not accept a client request to bypass quarantine/private-corpus rules merely because the client can name a path.\\n\\n### 4. Mersearch clients\\n\\n**Research frontend:** advanced query bar, filters/facets, chronology, provenance cards, explain-match, source-family handling, equation views, saved queries, export.\\n\\n**Conversation Viewer:** message-level retrieval/jump targets and conversation-local/global search using the same semantics where practical.\\n\\n**Glass Sausage Factory / public site:** public-profile search only. The site is a client, not an independent search authority.\\n\\n**Worker/automation clients:** JSON/JSONL/CSV/CLI/API access for reproducible research, batch archaeology and generated indexes.\\n\\n## Corpus / capability profiles\\n\\nProfiles define permitted corpus and expensive capabilities, not different meanings for the same query.\\n\\n- **public** — only material explicitly available to the public/site.\\n- **viewer** — material legitimately exposed through the Viewer.\\n- **worker** — permitted project corpus for ordinary workers; quarantine and PRIOR_ART remain excluded unless a separately authorized lane/profile exists.\\n- **admin/maintenance** — diagnostics and index maintenance; access still follows repository/quarantine policy.\\n\\nProfile names do not themselves grant access. Enforcement belongs server/index side.\\n\\n## Query language — current\\n\\nUnqualified terms search record body text.\\n\\nCurrent fields:\\n- `body:` — explicit body phrase/term.\\n- `math:` — conservative notation-normalized mathematical substring search.\\n- `name:` — basename; supports shell-style `*`, `?`, character classes.\\n- `path:` — source path; same glob support.\\n- `ext:` — extension, without leading dot.\\n- `type:` / `kind:` — indexed record kind.\\n- `has:` — mechanically established properties such as conversation-source, pdf-source, text-source, message-id, conversation-id, viewer.\\n- `author:` / `speaker:`\\n- `role:`\\n- `title:`\\n- `conversation:` / `cid:`\\n- `date:` including `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD`\\n- `status:` — lexical status-signal retrieval only.\\n\\nExamples:\\n\\n```text\\nname:*2026.txt\\nname:*26.txt OR name:26*.txt\\n(path:*SAT_CONVOS_20* AND ext:txt) AND body:\\\"star shaped\\\"\\nauthor:Nathan AND (holonomy NEAR/12 glitch)\\nmath:\\\"B=3/(4*pi)\\\"\\n```\\n\\n## Mathematical retrieval roadmap\\n\\n### M0 — notation normalization — IMPLEMENTED\\n\\nNormalize common presentation differences while preserving raw source:\\n- selected Unicode/LaTeX/plain symbol aliases;\\n- multiplication/division glyphs;\\n- Unicode minus / approximation;\\n- whitespace;\\n- simple LaTeX fractions.\\n\\nA notation match is **not algebraic equivalence**. Current negative acceptance control requires `math:\\\"4*pi*B=3\\\"` not to match `B=3/(4*pi)` merely because a human can rearrange it.\\n\\n### M1 — expression extraction\\n\\nIdentify probable equation spans from LaTeX delimiters, display blocks, inline formulas, Unicode/plain equations and code-like math. Store:\\n- exact raw expression;\\n- source locator;\\n- surrounding context;\\n- notation-normalized form;\\n- parse status;\\n- parser/version.\\n\\nNever discard `UNPARSED` expressions.\\n\\n### M2 — structural parsing\\n\\nParse supported expressions into a symbolic AST. Add:\\n- `contains:` structural/subexpression search;\\n- symbol/function/operator facets;\\n- equation-shape fingerprints;\\n- alpha-renaming option only when explicitly requested.\\n\\n### M3 — algebraic relation\\n\\nAdd conservative CAS-backed relationship testing:\\n- `EXACT`\\n- `NORMALIZED-EQUIVALENT`\\n- `ALGEBRAICALLY-EQUIVALENT`\\n- `CONTAINS-SUBEXPRESSION`\\n- `NUMERICALLY-CONSISTENT`\\n- `POSSIBLE-RELATION`\\n- `UNPARSED`\\n\\nTarget query: `equiv:\\\"B=3/(4*pi)\\\"`.\\n\\nCAS transformations must be recorded and bounded. Timeouts/failures remain visible. Do not silently equate expressions under unstated domain assumptions.\\n\\n### M4 — equation genealogy / derivation archaeology\\n\\nTarget `derive:` searches documented archive relationships rather than inventing a derivation. Desired chain:\\n`first known occurrence → reformulation → substitution → numerical evaluation → cross-sector reuse → correction/reversal → latest known occurrence`.\\n\\nChronology alone never establishes supersession. Explicit source language and provenance review control those labels.\\n\\n## Research-power roadmap\\n\\n### High priority\\n\\n1. **Facets and counts:** author, role, year/date, extension, kind, conversation, topic, status signal, source family.\\n2. **File-level inventory mode:** avoid returning one filename match per record/message when the research question is about files.\\n3. **Pagination/cursors and stable total-hit count:** current `--limit` truncates after sorting and should not be confused with total matches.\\n4. **Stable API schema:** separate request, response metadata, facets and hits.\\n5. **Duplicate/snapshot awareness:** attach established conversation-family relation classes; never infer canonical/newest/preferred.\\n6. **Saved/named queries:** versioned query + profile + sort + topic config + index/source identity.\\n7. **Explain-search:** human-readable and structured reason each hit matched.\\n8. **Regex mode:** explicit opt-in, bounded and clearly distinguished from literal search.\\n9. **Case control:** explicit sensitive/insensitive behavior.\\n10. **Prefix/wildcard/fuzzy lexical modes:** explicit, never silently applied.\\n11. **Neighbor-message proximity:** distinguish within-record `NEAR` from message-window proximity.\\n12. **Chronology/history mode:** first/latest occurrence, density and candidate correction/supersession signals without automatic authority inference.\\n13. **Exports:** JSON, JSONL, CSV, Markdown, TSV/plain-text; reproducibility manifest.\\n14. **Source representation graph:** PDF ↔ proven text extraction ↔ rendered/reader version; heuristic candidate relations must be labeled heuristic.\\n15. **Public-safe search profile:** required before live-site backend exposure.\\n\\n### Later / heavier\\n\\n- stemming/lemmatization as opt-in;\\n- multilingual/tokenization improvements;\\n- typo/fuzzy ranking;\\n- semantic/vector retrieval as a separately labeled retrieval mode;\\n- concept graph / topic adjacency;\\n- equation structural and CAS layers;\\n- citation/bibliographic entity search;\\n- image/figure metadata search;\\n- incremental indexing and cache invalidation;\\n- query-performance telemetry without leaking private query/source data;\\n- authenticated research API;\\n- rate limiting and resource budgets;\\n- UI query builder and syntax highlighting.\\n\\n## Provenance / explain contract\\n\\nEvery substantive hit should be able to answer:\\n1. What exact source object matched?\\n2. What corpus/profile allowed it?\\n3. What exact query clause matched?\\n4. Where in the record did it match?\\n5. What normalization/transformation, if any, occurred?\\n6. What source hash/ref/index version was searched?\\n7. Is the displayed source original, extraction, generated representation, or heuristic relation?\\n8. Is any status label lexical, source-authored, reviewed, or inferred?\\n\\nA numeric relevance score without this information is insufficient for research use.\\n\\n## Source relationships\\n\\nDo not infer `PDF → TXT export` solely from similar filenames. Relations may be:\\n- **PROVEN** — explicit manifest/provenance/tool output.\\n- **CONTENT-VERIFIED** — independently compared content establishes the relation.\\n- **CANDIDATE** — basename/path/metadata suggests a relation.\\n- **NONE/UNKNOWN**.\\n\\nClients must be able to distinguish them.\\n\\n## Duplicate / snapshot policy\\n\\nUse the established conversation-relation axes and sidecar work. Search presentation may group related exports, but grouping must not:\\n- delete or hide unique branch material;\\n- call the newest/largest/LIVE copy authoritative;\\n- silently suppress a branch;\\n- convert byte identity into semantic/currentness authority.\\n\\nExpose relation class and allow expand/collapse.\\n\\n## Security / boundary rules\\n\\n- Default exclusions include `QUARANTINE` and `PRIOR_ART`.\\n- Public clients use an allowlisted public corpus/profile, not merely a denylist.\\n- Do not expose filesystem/repository secrets, private paths or hidden source excerpts through error messages/facets.\\n- Regex/CAS/fuzzy/semantic operations require bounded resource budgets.\\n- Query logs, if retained, are operational data and need an explicit retention/privacy rule.\\n- Backend responses must escape/render source text safely; source text is data, never executable markup.\\n- API/client cannot override server-side corpus policy.\\n\\n## Testing\\n\\nThe existing GitHub Actions acceptance gate compiles Core and runs deterministic synthetic semantics tests. Every query-language change should add a positive and negative fixture. Maintain regression tests for:\\n- precedence;\\n- quoted Unicode;\\n- NEAR boundaries/distances;\\n- field parsing;\\n- globs;\\n- exclusion policy;\\n- math normalization and false-equivalence controls.\\n\\nAdd future fixture families for inventory dedup, pagination totals, API schema, duplicate-family annotations, source relations, regex resource limits, and symbolic math assumptions.\\n\\n## Current implementation status — 2026-09-20\\n\\nRuntime-green before this document:\\n- Boolean/implicit Boolean/parentheses;\\n- phrases;\\n- NEAR;\\n- author/role/title/date/CID/status fields;\\n- body/name/path/ext/kind/has fields;\\n- filename/path globs;\\n- Unicode quoted fields;\\n- sorting;\\n- default quarantine/PRIOR_ART exclusions;\\n- conservative math notation normalization;\\n- JSON/JSONL/CSV/Markdown outputs;\\n- topic co-occurrence enrichment;\\n- provenance/explanation traces.\\n\\nFirst bounded real-corpus smoke run has been launched through the repo-native acceptance workflow; at last check it was delayed in GitHub checkout and had not yet reached the corpus-query steps. A new kind of cyclic universe\n   ID: y2u6cp6320bn\n   2022 · Ijjas, Anna, Steinhardt, Paul J.\n   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.1904.08022\n   Abstract: Combining intervals of ekpyrotic (ultra-slow) contraction with a (non-singular) classical bounce naturally leads to a novel cyclic theory of the universe in which the Hubble parameter, energy density and temperature oscillate periodically, but the scale factor grows by an exponential factor from one cycle to the next. The resulting cosmology not only resolves the homogeneity, isotropy, flatness and monopole problems and generates a nearly scale invariant spectrum of density perturbations, but it also addresses a number of age-old cosmological issues that big bang inflationary cosmology does not. There may also be wider-ranging implications for fundamental physics, black holes and quantum measurement. \n\n2. The Cyclic Universe: From Planck Scale to Cosmic scale of the Universe\n   ID: 5nb20c64513s\n   2025 · Amrit Ladhani\n   DOI: 10.20944/preprints202207.0121.v11\n   Abstract: This paper proposes a novel cyclic cosmological model characterized by finite Planck and Cosmic scales. Unlike conventional models, this framework introduces a repulsive force arising from the extreme compression of spacetime. Spacetime quantization, as suggested by loop quantum gravity, plays a crucial role in this process. As the universe contracts, the compression of discrete spacetime units stores energy, which is subsequently released, driving expansion. The model predicts a transition from deceleration to acceleration, determined by the interplay between gravity and this repulsive force. Mathematical derivations are presented to estimate the Maximum Cosmic Scale and Maximum Time based on fundamental constants. The model’s predictions will be compared with observational data, including Type Ia supernovae, to assess its compatibility with current cosmological observations. This model offers a potential alternative to dark energy in explaining cosmic acceleration. \n\n3. Cyclic universe theory\n   ID: 1e7ag549ih\n   2009 · Paul J. The Cyclic Universe Model: A Theory of Cosmic Evolution Driven by Intrinsic Steady-State Attraction\n   ID: opdlvkh35lr7\n   2025\n   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.16902228\n   Abstract: This paper presents a unified theory of cosmic evolution based on the fundamentalprinciple of Intrinsic Steady-State Attraction (ISSA) inherent to all quantum particles andmatter. We propose that the Universe undergoes eternal cycles of expansion andcontraction, driven by this inherent drive towards stability. The Big Bang is explained asthe explosive rebound following the gravitational collapse of a prior universe'sultra-massive black hole, whose core reached a critical pressure threshold.Post-explosion, matter, governed by ISSA, aggregates into hierarchical stable structures– from fundamental particles forming stable elements (as cataloged in the periodictable), to compounds, planets, stars, galaxies, and ultimately, large-scale structures. Thegravitational force itself is posited as a macroscopic manifestation of this fundamentalparticle-level attraction towards stability and larger mass concentrations. Celestialevolution (planets to stars, stars to compact objects, compact objects to black holes) isdriven by continuous accretion fueled by ISSA/gravity. Ultimately, a supermassive blackhole, accreting surrounding material to a point where its core exceeds a critical pressurelimit, collapses into a singularity, triggering the next Big Bang and initiating a new cosmiccycle. Non-steady-state configurations are inherently unstable and transient. ThisISSA-driven model provides a comprehensive explanation for the origin of the Universe,the formation of all structures, the nature of gravity, and the perpetual cosmic cycle. \n\n5. Циклическая Вселенная: между теоретической моделью и наблюдательными свидетельствами\n   ID: sle50xyukwmo\n   2025 · Светлана Крюкова\n   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18107294\n   Abstract: В работе исследуется соответствие модели циклической Вселенной совре-менным наблюдательным данным. Анализируются ключевые теоретическиеположения, сопоставляются предсказания модели с результатами астрономиче-ских наблюдений. Особое внимание уделено механизмам, разрешающим фун-даментальные проблемы космологии (происхождение времени, энтропия ран-ней Вселенной, природа тёмной энергии). Представлены способы эмпирическойпроверки гипотезы через анализ крупномасштабной структуры Вселенной и ре-ликтового излучения.В дополнении приведён обзор математических формализмов, симуляцииидей циклической модели с использованием языка программирования Python,а также анализ степени соответствия модели текущим данным (до 92–95 %).Предложена новая интерпретация гравитационных волн как возможных марке-ров межцикловых переходов с интеграцией концепций квантовой гравитации. \n\n6. Циклическая Вселенная: между теоретической моделью и наблюдательными свидетельствами\n   ID: s818yqhwda1s\n   2025 · Светлана Крюкова\n   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18107293\n   Abstract: В работе исследуется соответствие модели циклической Вселенной совре-менным наблюдательным данным. Анализируются ключевые теоретическиеположения, сопоставляются предсказания модели с результатами астрономиче-ских наблюдений. Особое внимание уделено механизмам, разрешающим фун-даментальные проблемы космологии (происхождение времени, энтропия ран-ней Вселенной, природа тёмной энергии). Представлены способы эмпирическойпроверки гипотезы через анализ крупномасштабной структуры Вселенной и ре-ликтового излучения.В дополнении приведён обзор математических формализмов, симуляцииидей циклической модели с использованием языка программирования Python,а также анализ степени соответствия модели текущим данным (до 92–95 %).Предложена новая интерпретация гравитационных волн как возможных марке-ров межцикловых переходов с интеграцией концепций квантовой гравитации. \n\n7. Quantum Cosmology as a Hydrogen atom: Discrete $Λ$ and cyclic Universes from Wheeler-DeWitt quantization\n   ID: mxy56wa37jp3\n   2026 · Dipayan Mukherjee, Harkirat Singh Sahota, S. Shankaranarayanan\n   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.2601.20286\n   Abstract: Building upon our recently established correspondence between quantum cosmology and the hydrogen atom [1], we investigate the specific sector of a negative cosmological constant ($Λ&lt; 0$) in a flat FLRW universe with dust. While the positive $Λ$ sector [1] yields a continuous spectrum and a single bounce, we show here that the negative $Λ$ sector leads to a discrete spectrum of energy eigenvalues, effectively quantizing the cosmological constant. Within this dual description, the operator-ordering ambiguity parameter appears as the azimuthal quantum number of the hydrogen atom. A skewed Bohr correspondence emerges for the bound states, matching classical evolution at large volumes but deviating near the bounce. By constructing wave packets from these bound states, we demonstrate that the classical Big Bang and Big Crunch singularities are resolved, and the universe oscillates between quantum bounces and classical turnaround points. The expectation values of the observables indicate a cyclic universe -- with vanishing Hubble parameter at turnarounds -- undergoing quantum bounces. This exactly solvable model offers a tractable setting to explore quantum gravitational effects in cosmology. We analyze the properties of this cyclic universe, contrasting its bound-state dynamics with the scattering states of the de Sitter case. \n\n8. A cyclic model of the universe\n   ID: 51dnq9u111\n   2002 · Paul J. Steinhardt, Neil Turok · Science\n   DOI: 10.1126/SCIENCE.1070462\n   Abstract: We propose a cosmological model in which the universe undergoes an endless sequence of cosmic epochs that begin with a “bang” and end in a “crunch.” Temperature and density at the transition remain finite. Instead of having an inflationary epoch, each cycle includes a period of slow accelerated expansion (as recently observed) followed by contraction that produces the homogeneity, flatness, and energy needed to begin the next cycle.\n\n9. A Cyclic Model of the Universe\n   ID: b52529s7d92v\n   2022 · Steinhardt, Paul J., Turok, Neil\n   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.hep-th/0111030\n   Abstract: We propose a cosmological model in which the universe undergoes an endless sequence of cosmic epochs each beginning with a `bang' and ending in a `crunch.' The temperature and density are finite at each transition from crunch to bang. Instead of having an inflationary epoch, each cycle includes a period of slow accelerated expansion (as recently observed) followed by slow contraction. The combination produces the homogeneity, flatness, density fluctuations and energy needed to begin the next cycle. \n\n10. Cyclic Cosmology Regulated by Time-Crystal Densities\n   ID: w6x50rpb4679\n   2025\n   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17565749\n   Abstract: Can the universe sustain endless cycles without singularities, thresholds, or fine-tuned resets? We demonstrate a cosmological model in which the universe evolves cyclically through successive phases of expansion and contraction, without singularities, or fine-tuned thresholds. Time-crystal-inspired energy densities – one decaying like radiation and one providing periodic modulation - are incorporated into the Friedmann equation. These components enable self-sustaining bounces and long-term dynamic stability. Numerical simulations confirm that the squared Hubble parameter, energy density, and scale factor remain bounded and strictly periodic across cycles. The result is a minimalist, physically grounded framework that offers a new route for cyclic cosmology consistent with current observational constraints. ",

We demonstrate a cosmological model in which the universe evolves cyclically through successive phases of expansion and contraction, without singularities, or fine-tuned thresholds. Time-crystal-inspired energy densities – one decaying like radiation and one providing periodic modulation - are incorporated into the Friedmann equation.
